Take Time is a cooperative game where players either win or lose together.

To succeed, you must strategically play 12 cards facedown around a Clock, following specific rules for each Test. You can work together through a series of games to pass all 40 Tests available in the game.

—description from the publisher
community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Crappy clone of The Mind and Bomb Busters, where you don’t talk. JUST COMPUTE THE CLOCK.

[Rating: 3/10] So dull. People like to compare this to The Mind, but The Mind is a much better game. That game has constant tension with every single card play. In Take Time, you just go around and play cards facedown, then flip them up and see if you won or not.  I was hoping the missions would throw some craziness into the mix to make the game more exciting, but they do not. The new rules are just things like "an even card can't be played here" and "only a 7-9 can be played here."  Since not all cards are dealt out, it's also possible to have an unwinnable round just based on the card distribution.  I play

[Rating: 3/10] Another limited communication coop game. This one did not work AT ALL for the groups I tried it with. No idea what we have missed, looking at the other reviews / ratings

[Rating: 3/10] There is no interest whatsoever in either the themeless theme or the uninspired card play mechanic. You play cards blindly without knowing what other have played or even could play in hope you put cards in ascending order...then rince and repeat. I felt like playing red or black. The production is very beautiful but this is a very shallow and boring game.

[Rating: 3/10] This game seemed excessively difficult with 4 players. Way to draw dependent. There was one mission that we did with all cards face up multiple times and still took us multiple tries.

[Rating: 3/10] Für mich klarer Verlierer im Gegensatz zu Spielen wie „TheGang“ the „TheMind“. Viel zu oft ergeben sich Situationen, in denen man nach dem Verlieren der Runde nachvollziehen kann, dass die Runde mit den Karten im Spiel nicht schaffbar war…  Viel zu wenig Planbarkeit und Taktik für mich ?‍♂️

[Rating: 3.5/10] Habe es zu viert gespielt. Mir hat es keinen Spaß gemacht. Mit den richtigen Personen und besseren Absprachen könnte es vielleicht mehr Spaß machen.

[Rating: 3.8/10] [i]Take Time[/i] is a 24-card activity masquerading as a game. It's what you pull out on a casual, low-stakes night when you want to feel like you're accomplishing a cooperative feat together, without the stress and pressure that comes with a true performance-driven cooperative game. Don't get [i]Take Time[/i] if you want a clever deduction game where skill trumps luck and success hinges on reasoning. This is more like [i]The Mind[/i]: all vibes and nothing else.  Read my comprehensive review: https://shelfgamer.com/reviews/take-time/

[Rating: 4/10] Co-Op card game which has beautiful material and looks really nice. Can be quite frustrating as the (only) three cards you have to play are random and therefore it´s quite luck dependent. If I want to play sth similar I will probably prefer The Crew or also Bomb Busters.   Update 2026: Don´t get the hype, I have the feeling the clocks are not well balanced and in my experience the game is creating quite a lot of frustration.

[Rating: 4/10] Chels: 4 Ant: 4  Eh, it's alright - the 'developed The Mind' style game is an alchemist's prize, and so difficult to achieve with the cleanliness that the original could muster. This tries and kind of succeeds, but not to the extent that we need to see more.

[Rating: 4/10] Not much better than the game. Would rather play the gang. The game at least has a small box to easily take with you.

[Rating: 4/10] I was super excited to get this as a follow-up to Bomb Busters to play with my daughter.  After the first level, I'm feeling a bit let down.  Hopefully the campaign picks up, but I don't see this coming close to the enjoyment we had with Bomb Busters.  After a few more plays, I'm adjusting my rating down.  After almost a decade in the hobby, I can usually predict whether or not I'll like a game.  Unfortunately, I was way off on this one.

[Rating: 4/10] Disclaimer, i dont like hidden info coop trick takers. But i dont see why this is going to get played if you already have The Crew or The Gang, score here is crazy inflated. Very hyped

[Rating: 4/10] we didnt have fun at all, card dependant, sometimes you cannot win if you dont get good cards for the mission, not for me at all

[Rating: 4/10] Really light cooperative experience.  Basically set up 'rules' before each round to help define what you (collectively) 'should' do.  Then basically hope that the cards dealt fit those rules, otherwise it's pretty much just a bit of guessing.  That's fine because it is SO short, anything longer would get frustrating real fast.  Overall a mild puzzle followed by fairly random card deal to see if it worked.  Fine, but not my jam.

[Rating: 4.5/10] Played through it and hated it at two players. Just too much randomness. A shame..
